objectiveFull: Review the audio generation + mastering pipeline of "Water Born", a static web storybook (Node 24, TypeScript run directly by Node type stripping). Intent: (1) generate paid ElevenLabs assets ONCE into committed `audio-src/` (narration per page via POST /v1/text-to-speech/{voice}/with-timestamps with model eleven_v4 and audio tags prepended to blocks — story text must stay verbatim; SFX via /v1/sound-generation; music via /v1/music) and never regenerate existing files because credits are limited; (2) `scripts/master-audio.ts` builds `public/audio/` from `audio-src/` with ONE static gain per file to LUFS targets (no dynamic compression so loops stay seamless) and writes per-page narration timing JSON mapping alignment character times onto each block's verbatim text; (3) the ElevenLabs API key lives only in `.env` (gitignored) and must never be logged, committed or shipped. Files: scripts/gen-audio.ts, scripts/master-audio.ts, scripts/narration.ts, scripts/narration-direction.ts, src/content/sound.ts, src/content/narration-timing.ts, tests/narration.test.ts, package.json scripts audio:gen/audio:master. Focus on correctness of the alignment→timing mapping (offsets, tag skipping, separator handling), failure behaviour that could waste paid credits or lose paid output, secret handling, and test adequacy. The binary mp3/json files under audio-src/ and public/audio/ are generated outputs; don't review their contents. Known and accepted: count-chime SFX is quiet (peak -13 dB after mastering), kept to save credits.

findings.issue: alimiter is used with ffmpeg's default latency=false, which per the ffmpeg docs delays output by the 5 ms attack lookahead and does not flush the last 5 ms at EOF; every loop file gets a dropout or click at its seam, and the limiter is dynamic gain reduction, against the one-static-gain intent.
findings.fix: Append :latency=1 to the alimiter arguments, or omit alimiter for loop and music targets (gain is normally negative there) so mastering is a pure static gain; then check one loop's sample count and seam against its source.

findings.issue: The narration skip requires both mp3 and alignment to exist, and the mp3 is written before the alignment (lines 50-51). A crash between the writes, or an undefined data.alignment making writeFileSync throw, leaves only the mp3; the next run pays again and overwrites the paid original, contradicting the 'never regenerated' header.
findings.fix: Validate audio_base64 and alignment before writing anything, and skip (or throw asking for manual deletion) when either file exists.

findings.issue: The timing test checks block 1's length and block 0's first time but never that block 1's first time equals offsets[1]/10, so separator and offset mapping in toTiming is not asserted directly; the empty-tag branch (narration.ts:25) is never exercised.
findings.fix: Add assert.equal(timing.blocks[1]!.at[0], input.offsets[1]! / 10) and a case with a '' tag.

findings.issue: The comment says the timing JSON is written by scripts/gen-audio.ts; it is written by scripts/master-audio.ts:73. Also scripts/narration-direction.ts:3 cites tests/narration-direction.test.ts, which does not exist (the check is in tests/narration.test.ts:8).
findings.fix: Correct both file references.

findings.issue: Comment cites tests/narration-direction.test.ts, which does not exist; the per-block direction check lives in tests/narration.test.ts:8-10.
findings.fix: Point the comment at tests/narration.test.ts.

findings.issue: Doc comment says the timing JSON is written by scripts/gen-audio.ts; it is written by scripts/master-audio.ts:73 (gen-audio only writes the raw alignment).
findings.fix: Change the comment to scripts/master-audio.ts.

findings.issue: The request-text derivation buildNarrationInput(page, DIRECTION[page.id] ?? []) is duplicated in scripts/gen-audio.ts:42, yet mastering must reproduce exactly what was sent or toTiming throws.
findings.fix: Add narrationInputFor(page) to scripts/narration.ts and call it from both scripts.

findings.issue: SFX and music mastering iterates readdirSync(src) and derives the id via string-replace, needing a separate loops Set and a nested ternary for the target; stale originals are shipped and catalogue ids with no original are silently skipped, unlike the narration loop which iterates book.pages.
findings.fix: Iterate Object.entries(SFX) and Object.entries(MUSIC) and take the target from spec directly; this drops the Set, the replace and the nested ternary.

findings.issue: Loop narrowing is hand-written twice in different forms ('loop' in spec ? spec.loop : false here, 'loop' in spec && spec.loop in master-audio.ts:56), only because Object.entries on an as-const object yields a union.
findings.fix: Use Object.entries<SfxSpec>(SFX) so spec.loop ?? false type-checks in both places.

findings.issue: Only block 0's first time is checked against its offset; block 1 gets a length check only, so a separator-length offset error in buildNarrationInput would pass the test.
findings.fix: Assert at[0] === offsets[i]/10 and at.length === block.text.length for every block, on a three-block page such as p02.

findings.issue: Log and error messages (lines 24, 28, 35, 45) use URL pathname, which shows %20 for the space in the project path and relies on splitting at '/audio/', even though a path() helper for decoded filesystem paths exists at line 20; the helper's name also reads like the node:path module.
findings.fix: Use the helper in messages and consider renaming it to fsPath.

findings.issue: Narration skip requires both mp3 and alignment to exist, and the mp3 is written first (line 50). Any throw after it (e.g. missing alignment makes writeFileSync(file, undefined) throw) leaves a lone mp3; the next run re-bills the page and overwrites the paid mp3, contradicting the never-regenerate contract in lines 1-2.
findings.fix: Validate audio_base64 and alignment.characters before writing either file, and skip when either file exists so a half pair fails loudly in audio:master instead of being silently re-billed.

findings.issue: toTiming checks only characters.join('') === input.text. Index slicing by UTF-16 offsets also assumes characters.length === text.length and character_start_times_seconds.length === characters.length; a multi-unit entry or short times array would silently shift or truncate the at arrays persisted from external API data.
findings.fix: Extend the existing guard to throw when alignment.characters.length !== input.text.length or the times array length differs from characters.length.

findings.issue: spawnSync launch failure (ENOENT) returns status null and stderr null; the status branch then calls run.stderr.slice and throws a TypeError that masks the real cause.
findings.fix: Add `if (run.error) throw run.error;` before the status check.

findings.issue: The header comment (lines 2-3) says one static gain and never dynamic processing so loops stay seamless, but the filter chain applies alimiter, a dynamic lookahead limiter.
findings.fix: Correct the comment to say a safety peak limiter follows the static gain, or drop or adjust the limiter (see open question on latency).

findings.issue: The 'skipping tags' timing test asserts the start time only for block 0 and only the length for block 1, so a wrong offset for later blocks (separator + tag prefix) would pass.
findings.fix: Assert timing.blocks[i].at[0] === input.offsets[i] / 10 for every block, or deepEqual the full blocks array.

findings.issue: Stale comments: this line cites tests/narration-direction.test.ts, which does not exist (check is in tests/narration.test.ts:8); src/content/narration-timing.ts:1 says the JSON is written by gen-audio.ts but master-audio.ts:73 writes it.
findings.fix: Point both comments at the real test file and the real writer script.

findings.issue: No retry or backoff on paid POSTs; this is correct because a retry could bill twice, and undici's default 300 s timeouts bound a hang.
findings.fix: None.

findings.issue: MAX_GAIN_DB clamp leaves very quiet sources below target without flagging the miss; consistent with the accepted quiet count-chime.
findings.fix: None.

findings.issue: Stale comment (out of security lens, readability): says tests/narration-direction.test.ts checks one direction per block, but that file does not exist; the check lives in tests/narration.test.ts:8-10.
findings.fix: Point the comment at tests/narration.test.ts.

findings.issue: Stale comment (out of security lens, readability): says public/audio/narration/<pageId>.json is written by scripts/gen-audio.ts, but scripts/master-audio.ts:73 writes it; gen-audio.ts only writes audio-src/*.alignment.json.
findings.fix: Change the comment to name scripts/master-audio.ts.

findings.issue: toTiming test asserts only block 1's length and block 0's first time; wrong offsets for blocks after the first (e.g. offsets[0] for all, or a dropped separator) still pass, and the untagged '' branch is never exercised.
findings.fix: For every page and block, deepEqual timing.blocks[i].at against (offsets[i]+k)/10 for k in 0..len-1; add a synthetic page with an empty tag.

findings.issue: No test ties the committed public/audio/narration/*.json or audio-src alignments to book.ts; editorial page/block changes leave stale timings with verify green, and monotonic 'at' (required by the spokenChars binary search) is never checked on real data.
findings.fix: Add a credit-free test: for each page, run toTiming on the committed alignment, deepEqual the blocks against the committed public JSON, and assert each 'at' is non-decreasing.

findings.issue: assert.throws has no matcher, so any exception passes; the ['x'] fixture differs in length and doesn't model a realistic same-length or tags-stripped mismatch.
findings.fix: Use assert.throws(fn, /does not match the request text/) with a same-length one-char-different or tag-less fixture.

findings.issue: spokenChars boundary at t equal to a start time is untested; changing <= to < in narration-timing.ts:15 would not fail any test.
findings.fix: Add assert.equal(spokenChars(at, 0.1), 2) and an empty-array case.

findings.issue: Comment cites tests/narration-direction.test.ts, which does not exist; the check is in tests/narration.test.ts:8-10.
findings.fix: Point the comment at tests/narration.test.ts.

findings.issue: Credit-protection skip logic and master-audio gain/target selection are untested; acceptable given they are one-line checks in side-effecting scripts and tag/block count mismatches throw before any paid call.
findings.fix: None required.
